qr.e: Width=54÷9=6; perimeter=2(9+6)=30.

y.A: 36 is 9 × 4, as if every side were 9. The width is 54 ÷ 9 = 6.
y.B: 24 is 9 + 9 + 3 + 3, going round a rectangle 9 by 3. This one is 9 by 6, because 54 ÷ 9 = 6.
y.D: 15 is 9 + 6, one length and one width. The perimeter is both pairs: 2 × 15 = 30.

qr.q: A triangle has two equal angles of 55°. What is the third angle?
The mean of 12, 14, 16, and x is 15. What is x?
qr.e: A mean of 15 for 4 numbers means total 60; 60−42=18.

qr.q: A spinner has 8 equal sections: 3 red, 3 blue, 2 green. What is the probability of NOT landing on green?
qr.e: 6 of 8 sections are not green: 6/8=3/4.

qr.q: A student doubles the number of pages read each week: 3, 6, 12, 24, ... . How many pages come next?
qr.e: Each term doubles, so 24×2=48 pages.

y.A: 30 is 24 + 6, adding an earlier week on. The pattern doubles each time: 24 × 2 = 48.
y.B: 36 is 12 + 24, the last two weeks added. They double rather than add: 48.
y.C: 60 is 12 + 48, one week too many added on. Doubling 24 gives 48.

qr.q: A supply count must be divisible by both 4 and 6. Which count works?
qr.e: 24÷4=6 and 24÷6=4, so 24 is divisible by both numbers.

y.B: 20 divides by 4 but not by 6. The count has to work for both: 24.
y.C: 18 divides by 6 but not by 4. The first that does both is 24.
y.D: 30 divides by 6 but not by 4. 24 divides by both: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

qr.q: A jar is 2/3 full. After 8 cups are removed, it is 1/3 full. What is the jar's full capacity?
qr.e: The removed 8 cups equals 1/3 of the jar, so full capacity is 24.

y.B: 12 is 24 ÷ 2, half the jar rather than the whole of it. The 8 cups taken out are a third of the jar, so the full jar holds 8 × 3 = 24 cups.

qr.q: A runner travels 7.5 miles in 1.5 hours. What is the average rate?

y.C: 6 is 7.5 − 1.5, the miles with the hours taken off them. A rate comes from dividing: 7.5 ÷ 1.5 = 5 miles each hour.
y.D: 9 is 7.5 + 1.5, the miles and the hours added together. A rate comes from dividing instead: 7.5 ÷ 1.5 = 5 miles each hour.

qr.q: A paint mixture uses blue and white in a 2:5 ratio. If 21 cups are mixed, how many cups are blue?
qr.e: There are 7 parts; 21÷7=3, so blue = 2×3 = 6.

y.A: 15 is the white share, 5 parts of 7. Blue is the other 2 parts: 6 cups.
y.C: 7 is 2 + 5, the number of parts rather than cups. Each part is 21 ÷ 7 = 3, so blue is 6.
y.D: 10 is 2 × 5, the two ratio numbers multiplied. Blue is 2 parts of 3 cups: 6.

qr.q: A 9-by-9 game board has 81 spaces. Which expression has the same value as the number of spaces?
qr.e: The board has 9²=81 spaces, and 3⁴=81.

qr.q: A square display uses 70 tiles. Between which two whole-number side lengths would its side lie?
qr.e: Because 8²=64 and 9²=81, √70 lies between 8 and 9.

qr.q: A number is divisible by 2, 3, and 5. Which could be the number?
qr.e: 30 is divisible by 2, 3, and 5.

qr.q: A fence-post pattern uses 4, 7, 13, and 25 posts. The increases double. How many posts come next?
qr.e: The increases are +3,+6,+12, so the next increase is +24 and 25+24=49.

qr.q: A rectangular prism is 6 by 5 by 4. If its height is cut in half, what is the new volume?
qr.e: Original volume is 120; halving height halves volume to 60.

y.B: 120 is 60 × 2, double the volume the question asks for — the prism before the height was cut. Halving the height halves the volume: 120 ÷ 2 = 60.
y.C: 30 is 6 × 5, two of the three measurements — one face of the prism, not a volume. Halving the height halves the whole volume: 120 ÷ 2 = 60.

qr.q: A square has perimeter 36 cm. What is its area?
qr.e: Each side is 9; area = 9² = 81.

y.B: 144 is 36 × 4, the whole perimeter multiplied by four rather than shared between the four sides. One side comes from 36 ÷ 4 = 9, and the area is 9 × 9 = 81 square centimetres.
y.C: 72 is 36 × 2, the perimeter doubled. One side comes from 36 ÷ 4 = 9, and the area is 9 × 9 = 81 square centimetres.

qr.q: A right-angle art frame has one angle of 38°. What is the other angle?
qr.e: A right angle totals 90°, so 90−38=52°.

qr.q: Five supply trays contain an average of 14 items. How many items are in the trays altogether?
qr.e: Total equals mean×number of trays: 14×5=70 items.

y.C: 84 is 70 + 14, the five trays' total with one more 14 added on the end. Five trays with a mean of 14 come to 14 × 5 = 70 items.
y.D: 56 is 14 × 4, four trays' worth rather than five. The total is the mean multiplied by all five trays: 14 × 5 = 70 items.

qr.q: The ordered values are 3, 6, 9, x, and 15. Which value of x keeps the median at 9?
qr.e: With x=12, the ordered list is 3,6,9,12,15, whose middle value is 9.

qr.q: A fair number cube is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
qr.e: The favorable outcomes are 5 and 6, so the probability is 2/6=1/3.

qr.q: A point at (-2,4) moves 5 units right. What is the new point?
qr.e: -2+5=3, so the point is (3,4).

qr.q: A 60-page book is read at 12 pages per day. After 3 days, what fraction of the book remains unread?
qr.e: 36 pages are read, leaving 24; 24/60=2/5.

qr.q: A box of 6 granola bars costs $3.00. At that rate, what is the cost of one granola bar?
qr.e: The 6 bars share the $3.00 evenly, so one bar costs $3.00 divided by 6 = $0.50.

y.A: 2.00 is 6 ÷ 3, the bars shared between the dollars rather than the other way round. One bar costs $3.00 ÷ 6 = $0.50.

qr.q: A necklace uses 2 red beads for every 3 white beads. The necklace has 6 red beads. How many white beads does it have?
qr.e: The 6 red beads make 3 groups of 2, and each group comes with 3 white beads, so there are 3 x 3 = 9 white beads.

y.A: 4 is 6 − 2. The 6 red beads make 3 groups of 2, and each group brings 3 white: 9.
y.B: 12 is 6 × 2, the red beads doubled. Three groups of 3 white beads make 9.
y.C: 5 is 2 + 3, one group of each colour. There are three groups here: 3 × 3 = 9.

qr.q: In a basket of red and green apples, the ratio of red apples to green apples is 3:4. Which statement must be true?
c: 3 out of every 4 apples are red.
There are exactly 3 red apples and 4 green apples.
4 out of every 7 apples are red.
3 out of every 7 apples are red.
qr.e: A 3:4 ratio means every group of 3 red apples comes with 4 green ones, so each group has 7 apples and 3 of those 7 are red.

qr.q: A drawing of a bookcase uses a scale of 1 inch to 2 feet. The bookcase is 3 inches tall in the drawing. How tall is the real bookcase?
qr.e: Each inch in the drawing stands for 2 feet, so 3 inches stands for 3 x 2 = 6 feet.

y.A: 12 is 6 × 2, twice the real height — what a drawing 6 inches tall would stand for, not one 3 inches tall. Each inch stands for 2 feet, so 3 inches stands for 3 × 2 = 6 feet.
y.C: 5 is 2 + 3, the two numbers in the question added together. The scale multiplies instead: each inch stands for 2 feet, so 3 × 2 = 6 feet.

qr.q: On a park map, 2 centimeters represents 25 meters. A walking path is 14 centimeters long on the map. How long is the real path?
qr.e: 14 centimeters is 7 groups of 2 centimeters, and each 2 centimeters stands for 25 meters, so the path is 7 x 25 = 175 meters.

y.B: 50 is 2 × 25, the two numbers of the scale multiplied together — what 4 centimetres on the map would stand for, not 14. The path's 14 centimetres make 7 groups of 2, so 7 × 25 = 175 metres.
y.C: 350 is 25 × 14, the whole map length multiplied by 25 — but 25 metres goes with every 2 centimetres, not with every 1. The 14 centimetres make 7 groups of 2, so 7 × 25 = 175 metres.

qr.q: A printer prints 8 pages every 20 seconds at a steady rate. How many pages does it print in 3 minutes?
qr.e: Three minutes is 180 seconds, which is 9 groups of 20 seconds, so the printer prints 9 x 8 = 72 pages.

y.A: 160 is 8 × 20, the pages multiplied by the seconds they take. Three minutes holds 9 lots of 20 seconds, so 9 × 8 = 72 pages.
y.D: 24 is 8 × 3, the pages in 20 seconds multiplied by the number of minutes. Three minutes holds 9 lots of 20 seconds, so 9 × 8 = 72 pages.

qr.q: A paint color mixes red, yellow, and white in the ratio 2:3:5. A painter uses 12 cups of yellow. How many cups of white are used?
qr.e: Yellow is 3 parts and equals 12 cups, so one part is 4 cups; white is 5 parts, or 5 x 4 = 20 cups.

y.C: 24 is 12 × 2, the yellow cups doubled — the 2 belongs to red's share, not to white's. One part is 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cups, so white's five parts come to 5 × 4 = 20.
y.D: 15 is 3 × 5, yellow's 3 parts multiplied by white's 5 parts, which counts no cups. Each part is 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cups, so white's five parts come to 5 × 4 = 20.

qr.q: A model train is built at a scale of 1 inch to 8 feet. The real engine is 60 feet long. How long is the model?
qr.e: Each inch of the model stands for 8 feet, so the model is 60 divided by 8 = 7 1/2 inches long.

qr.q: A 15-ounce jar of honey costs $4.50. A 24-ounce jar of the same honey costs $6.72. Which jar is the better buy, and by how much per ounce?
c: The two jars cost the same per ounce
qr.e: $4.50 divided by 15 is $0.30 per ounce and $6.72 divided by 24 is $0.28 per ounce, so the 24-ounce jar saves $0.02 on every ounce.

qr.q: A recipe for 6 servings uses 3/4 cup of rice. Nadia has 2 cups of rice and plenty of everything else. What is the greatest number of whole servings she can make?
qr.e: One serving uses (3/4) divided by 6 = 1/8 cup, and 2 divided by 1/8 is 16, so she can make 16 servings.

y.B: 12 is 3 × 4, using the numbers of the fraction. One serving takes an eighth of a cup, so 2 cups make 16.
y.C: 14 is 16 − 2, two servings short. Each serving is an eighth of a cup, and 2 cups hold 16 of those.
y.D: 18 is 6 × 3. Six servings take three quarters of a cup, so one takes an eighth, and 2 cups make 16.

qr.q: Ana stacks 24 boxes in 40 minutes. Ben stacks 21 boxes in 35 minutes. Each works at a steady rate. Which statement is true?
c: They stack at the same rate.
Ana stacks twice as fast as Ben.
qr.e: Ana stacks 24 divided by 40 = 0.6 box per minute and Ben stacks 21 divided by 35 = 0.6 box per minute, so their rates are equal.

qr.q: A scale drawing of a soccer field shows the field as a rectangle 12 centimeters long and 8 centimeters wide. What is the actual length of the field?
c: There is not enough information to tell.
qr.e: No scale is given, so there is nothing to tell how many meters each centimeter of the drawing stands for.

qr.q: A number pattern starts at 4 and adds 5 each time: 4, 9, 14, 19, ... . What is the next number in the pattern?
qr.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before it, so the next number is 19 + 5 = 24.

y.A: 23 is 19 + 4, the last number plus the first one. The pattern adds 5 each time: 19 + 5 = 24.
y.D: 25 is 5 × 5, the step multiplied by itself. The step is added on instead: 19 + 5 = 24.

qr.q: Four bags of apples weigh 5 pounds, 7 pounds, 8 pounds, and 8 pounds. What is the mean weight of a bag?
qr.e: The four bags weigh 5 + 7 + 8 + 8 = 28 pounds in all, and 28 divided by 4 is 7 pounds.

y.B: 28 is 7 × 4, the four bags' weight altogether rather than the weight of one bag. The mean shares that total out: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 pounds.

qr.q: A backpack costs $40. During a sale the price drops 15%, and then a $5 coupon is used on the sale price. What is the final price?
qr.e: 15% of $40 is $6, so the sale price is $34, and $34 - $5 = $29.

y.C: 35 is 40 − 5, the coupon taken off the full price with the sale drop still to come. The 15% comes off first, bringing $40 down to $34, and then $34 − $5 = $29.

qr.q: A bag holds 3 red tiles and 5 green tiles. One tile is drawn without looking. What is the probability that it is red?
qr.e: There are 3 + 5 = 8 tiles in all and 3 of them are red, so the probability is 3/8.

qr.q: A faucet fills a 3-gallon bucket in 4 minutes at a steady rate. How many minutes does it take to fill a 27-gallon tub?
qr.e: 27 gallons is 9 buckets of 3 gallons, and each bucket takes 4 minutes, so it takes 9 x 4 = 36 minutes.

y.B: 108 is 4 × 27, the four minutes multiplied by every gallon rather than by every bucket. The 27 gallons make 9 buckets of 3, so the time is 9 × 4 = 36 minutes.
y.D: 9 is 27 ÷ 3, the number of 3-gallon buckets in the tub, not the minutes they take. Each bucket takes 4: 9 × 4 = 36.

qr.q: Of the 48 books on a shelf, 5/8 are novels. Of those novels, 2/5 are mysteries. How many of the books are mystery novels?
qr.e: 5/8 of 48 is 30 novels, and 2/5 of 30 is 12 mystery novels.

y.B: 10 is 5 × 2, the two top numbers of the fractions multiplied together, which counts no books. Take five eighths of the forty-eight first — that is 30 novels — then two fifths of those 30: 12.

qr.q: Five plants were measured: 6 cm, 9 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm, and 5 cm. What is the median height?
qr.e: In order the heights are 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 cm, and the middle one of the five is 6 cm.

qr.q: Two friends share $84 in the ratio 3:4. How much more money does the friend with the larger share receive?
qr.e: Seven equal parts make $84, so each part is $12; the shares are $36 and $48, and the difference is one part, $12.

y.A: 7 is 3 + 4, the number of parts rather than an amount. Each part is 84 ÷ 7 = 12, and the shares differ by one part.
y.C: 24 is 12 × 2, two parts. The shares are 36 and 48, which are one part apart: 12.
y.D: 48 is the larger share itself, not the gap between them: 48 − 36 = 12.

qr.q: Three corners of a rectangle are at (1, 1), (9, 1), and (9, 6). Where is the fourth corner?
qr.e: The side from (1, 1) to (9, 1) is horizontal and the side from (9, 1) to (9, 6) is vertical, so the fourth corner sits directly above (1, 1) at (1, 6).

qr.q: A pitcher holds 3 1/2 quarts of lemonade. Each glass holds 2/5 quart. How many full glasses can be poured, and how much lemonade is left over?
qr.e: 3 1/2 divided by 2/5 = 7/2 x 5/2 = 35/4 = 8 3/4, so 8 full glasses are poured, using 16/5 = 3 1/5 quarts and leaving 3 1/2 - 3 1/5 = 3/10 quart.

qr.q: Three times a number, decreased by 7, equals 26. What is half of that number?
qr.e: If 3n - 7 = 26, then 3n = 33 and n = 11, so half the number is 5 1/2.

qr.q: A rectangular box measures 12 cm by 8 cm by 6 cm. How many 2-cm cubes fit inside it exactly?
qr.e: Along the edges 6, 4, and 3 cubes fit (12/2, 8/2, and 6/2), so 6 x 4 x 3 = 72 cubes fill the box.

y.A: 36 is 72 ÷ 2, half the cubes. Along the edges 6, 4 and 3 fit, so 6 × 4 × 3 = 72.
y.B: 144 is 72 × 2, twice as many as fit. Halve each edge first, because the cubes are 2 cm.
y.C: 48 is 8 × 6, two of the box’s sides in centimetres. Count cubes along each edge instead.

qr.q: On a floor plan, 3 inches represents 4 feet. A room is 18 feet long. How long is that room on the plan?
qr.e: 18 feet is 4.5 groups of 4 feet, and each 4 feet is drawn as 3 inches, so the room is 4.5 x 3 = 13 1/2 inches long.

qr.q: Kara's first four quiz scores have a mean of 78. What must she score on her fifth quiz to raise her mean to 80?
qr.e: Four quizzes with mean 78 total 312, and five quizzes with mean 80 must total 400, so the fifth score is 400 - 312 = 88.

qr.q: A rectangular garden is 8 meters by 15 meters. A path 1 meter wide is built all the way around the outside of the garden. What is the area of the path alone?
qr.e: With the path, the outer rectangle is 10 m by 17 m, or 170 square meters; subtracting the garden's 8 x 15 = 120 square meters leaves 50 square meters.

y.C: 23 is 8 + 15, the garden's two sides added together — a length, not an area. With the path the outer rectangle measures 10 by 17, so 170 − 120 = 50 square metres.

qr.q: What is the next multiple of 8 after 40?
qr.e: The multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, so the next one after 40 is 48.

y.B: 56 is 48 + 8, one multiple of 8 further on than the one asked for. Counting on by 8 from 40 gives 40 + 8 = 48 first.

qr.q: Which is the best estimate of 6,127 divided by 29?
qr.e: 6,127 is about 6,000 and 29 is about 30, and 6,000 divided by 30 is 200.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is a prime number?
qr.e: 17 has no whole-number factors except 1 and itself, while 9 = 3 x 3, 15 = 3 x 5, and 21 = 3 x 7.

qr.q: In the number 47,205, the value of the digit 4 is how many times the value of the digit 2?
qr.e: The 4 stands for 40,000 and the 2 stands for 200, and 40,000 divided by 200 is 200.

y.C: 2 is 4 ÷ 2, the two digits divided rather than the values they stand for. The 4 stands for 40,000 and the 2 stands for 200, and 40,000 ÷ 200 = 200.

qr.q: Two consecutive whole numbers add up to 15. What is the larger of the two numbers?
qr.e: Consecutive whole numbers are 1 apart, and 7 + 8 = 15, so the larger number is 8.

y.A: 7 is 15 − 8, the smaller of the two numbers that add to 15. The question asks for the larger of the pair, which is 8.

qr.q: What is the sum of all the different prime factors of 210?
A student multiplied 397 x 18 and wrote 5,146. Without finding the exact product, which is the best reason to know that answer is wrong?
c: The product must be less than 4,000.
The product must end in the digit 7.
The product should be close to 7,200, not 5,146.
The product must be odd, and 5,146 is even.
qr.e: 397 is close to 400 and 400 x 18 = 7,200, so an answer near 5,100 is far too small; the exact product is 7,146.

qr.q: The four-digit number 73_4 is missing the digit in its tens place. If the number is divisible by 9, what is the missing digit?
qr.e: A number is divisible by 9 when its digits add to a multiple of 9; 7 + 3 + 4 = 14, and 14 + 4 = 18, so the missing digit is 4 and the number is 7,344.

y.D: 5 is 9 − 4, the 9 the number has to divide by take away the 4 it ends in. What counts is the total of the digits: the ones already there make 7 + 3 + 4 = 14, and 14 + 4 = 18, a multiple of 9.

qr.q: A whole number rounds to 4,600 when it is rounded to the nearest hundred. What is the greatest whole number it could be?
qr.e: Whole numbers from 4,550 through 4,649 round to 4,600, and 4,650 would round up to 4,700, so the greatest is 4,649.

qr.q: Which of these numbers has exactly three different whole-number factors?
qr.e: 49 has only the factors 1, 7, and 49; 15 and 21 each have four factors, and 64 has seven.

qr.q: A whole number multiplied by itself equals 729. What is the number?
The sum of three whole numbers is odd. Which statement must be true?
c: Exactly two of the numbers are even.
Exactly one of the numbers is odd.
At least one of the numbers is odd.
qr.e: If all three numbers were even the sum would be even, so at least one must be odd; the sum is odd when either one number or all three are odd.

qr.q: Which of these fractions is equal to 1/2?
qr.e: 5/10 means 5 out of 10, which is exactly half; 2/5 and 3/8 are each less than half, and 4/6 is more than half.

qr.q: A theater has 80 seats, and 10% of them are already sold. How many seats are sold?
qr.e: 10% is the same as one tenth, and one tenth of 80 seats is 8 seats.

y.A: 10 is the per cent itself, not a number of seats. A tenth of 80 seats is 8.
y.C: 18 is 10 + 8. Ten per cent means one tenth, so 80 ÷ 10 = 8 seats.
y.D: 40 is 80 ÷ 2, which would be fifty per cent. Ten per cent of 80 is 8.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 6 but NOT by 9?
qr.e: 132 is even and its digits add to 6, a multiple of 3, so it is divisible by 6, but 6 is not a multiple of 9.

qr.q: What is the value of 2 x 2 x 2 x 5?
qr.e: Multiplying step by step, 2 x 2 = 4, then 4 x 2 = 8, and 8 x 5 = 40.

y.C: 20 is 5 × 4, the 5 multiplied by two of the 2s. There is a third 2 still to use: 20 × 2 = 40.

qr.q: A theater has 48 rows with 32 seats in each row. Which is the closest estimate of the total number of seats?
qr.e: 48 is about 50 and 32 is about 30, so the total is about 50 x 30 = 1,500; the exact product is 1,536.

qr.q: The mean of five numbers is 24. The number 40 is removed from the set. What is the mean of the four numbers that remain?
qr.e: Five numbers with mean 24 total 120; removing 40 leaves 80, and 80 divided by 4 is 20.

y.C: 16 is 40 − 24, the number removed take away the old mean. The totals are what move here: the five numbers add to 120, then 120 − 40 = 80 and 80 ÷ 4 = 20.

qr.q: In a triangle, one angle is a right angle and the other two angles measure 3x degrees and 2x degrees. What is the value of x?
qr.e: The three angles total 180 degrees, so 3x + 2x + 90 = 180, which gives 5x = 90 and x = 18.

y.A: 20 is 2 + 18. The three angles make 180, so 5x + 90 = 180 and x = 18.
y.C: 15 is 18 − 3. Take the right angle off first: 5x = 90, so x = 18.
y.D: 36 is 18 × 2, which is the 2x angle rather than x. x itself is 18.

qr.q: A set of five whole numbers has a median of 7 and a range of 5. The smallest number is 5. What is the largest number?
c: There is not enough information to tell.
qr.e: The range is the largest number minus the smallest, so the largest is 5 + 5 = 10; the median does not change that.

y.A: 12 is 7 + 5, the median added to the range. The range is measured from the smallest number, not the middle one: 5 + 5 = 10.

qr.q: A model car is built at 1/24 of the size of the real car. The model is 7 inches long. How long is the real car, in feet?
qr.e: The real car is 24 x 7 = 168 inches long, and 168 divided by 12 is 14 feet.

y.A: 168 is 24 × 7, the real car's length in inches. The answer is wanted in feet, and 168 ÷ 12 = 14.

qr.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
qr.e: 5/8 = 0.625 and 2/3 is about 0.667, so the correct order is 0.6, then 5/8, then 2/3, then 0.7.

qr.q: A machine fills 350 bottles in 25 minutes at a steady rate. At that rate, how many bottles does it fill in 1 hour and 20 minutes?
qr.e: 350 divided by 25 is 14 bottles per minute, and 1 hour 20 minutes is 80 minutes, so 80 x 14 = 1,120 bottles.

y.B: 1,400 is 350 × 4, the bottles filled in four lots of 25 minutes — 100 minutes in all. An hour and twenty minutes is 80 minutes: 350 ÷ 25 = 14 a minute, and 14 × 80 = 1,120.

qr.q: A jacket costs $60. The store raises the price by 25%, then later takes 20% off the new price. What is the final price?
qr.e: A 25% increase makes the price $75, and 20% of $75 is $15, so the final price is $75 - $15 = $60.

qr.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 square centimeters and a perimeter of 36 centimeters. What are its side lengths?
qr.e: The two sides must add to 18, half of the perimeter, and multiply to 72; 6 + 12 = 18 and 6 x 12 = 72.

qr.q: When a whole number is divided by 7, the remainder is 4. What is the remainder when twice that number is divided by 7?
qr.e: Doubling adds the remainder to itself: 4 + 4 = 8, and 8 is one more than 7, so the new remainder is 1 (for example, 11 leaves 4 and 22 leaves 1).

y.A: 8 is 4 × 2, the doubled remainder before it is divided again. 8 is one more than 7, so the remainder is 1.
y.C: 2 is 4 ÷ 2, halving the remainder instead of doubling it. Doubling gives 8, which leaves 1.
y.D: 4 is the remainder before doubling. Twice the number leaves 8, and 8 − 7 = 1.

qr.q: Which of these statements is FALSE?
c: The product of two even numbers is always divisible by 8.
The sum of an even number and an odd number is always odd.
The sum of two odd numbers is always even.
The product of two odd numbers is always odd.
qr.e: 2 x 2 = 4, which is not divisible by 8, so the last statement is false; the other three are always true.

qr.q: A square photo frame has sides that are 7 inches long. What is the perimeter of the frame?
qr.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 × 7 = 28 inches.

y.A: 21 is 28 − 7, three sides. A square has four: 4 × 7 = 28.
y.C: 14 is 7 × 2, two sides. All four make the perimeter.
y.D: 49 is 7 × 7, the area — the space inside, not the distance round the edge.

qr.q: A box is filled with unit cubes. Each layer holds 8 cubes, and the box is 3 layers tall. How many unit cubes does the box hold in all?
qr.e: Three layers of 8 cubes each is 3 × 8 = 24 cubes.

y.A: 16 is 8 × 2, two layers. The box is three layers tall.
y.B: 32 is 8 × 4, four layers. There are three: 3 × 8 = 24.
y.D: 11 is 8 + 3. The layers multiply, they do not add.

qr.q: A rectangular tank is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 6 inches deep. Water in it is 3 inches deep. How many more cubic inches of water are needed to fill the tank?
qr.e: The tank holds 8×5×6=240 cubic inches and already has 8×5×3=120, so 240−120=120 more are needed.

y.B: 240 is 120 × 2, the whole tank filled right to the top. The tank already holds 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 cubic inches of water, so only 240 − 120 = 120 more are needed.
y.D: 40 is 8 × 5, the floor of the tank — the space it covers, not the water it holds. The depth still to fill is 3 inches: 8 × 5 × 3 = 120.

qr.q: The ages of nine students are listed in order: 8, 9, 9, 10, 10, 11, 11, 12, 13. What is the median age?
qr.e: With nine values listed in order, the median is the 5th one, and the 5th age in the list is 10.

qr.q: A shop records books sold: Monday 12, Tuesday 18, Wednesday 9, Thursday 15, Friday 21. The goal was to average 16 books per day over the five days. How many more books would the shop have had to sell that week to meet the goal?
qr.e: The shop sold 12+18+9+15+21=75 books, but the goal needed 5×16=80, so it fell 5 books short.

y.A: 16 is the goal for one day, not the shortfall. Five days need 5 × 16 = 80, and 80 − 75 = 5.
y.B: 25 is 5 × 5. The shop sold 75 against a goal of 80, so it was 5 short.
y.C: 1 is 16 − 15, one day compared. Add all five: 75 sold against 80 needed.

qr.q: One week of daily high temperatures has a range of 14°. The next week, every daily high is exactly 5° warmer than the matching day of the first week. What is the range of the second week's highs?
qr.e: Adding 5° to every value raises the highest and the lowest by the same amount, so the range stays 14°.

y.B: 9 is 14 − 5, the old range with the 5 taken off it. The 5 is added to every day alike, so the highest and the lowest move together and the range stays 14°.
y.D: 19 is 14 + 5, the range with the extra 5 added on. Both the highest and the lowest go up by 5, so the gap between them does not change: still 14°.

qr.q: In a pictograph, one book symbol stands for 8 books read. Grade 4 shows 5 1/2 symbols and Grade 5 shows 7 symbols. How many more books did Grade 5 read than Grade 4?
qr.e: Grade 5 read 7×8=56 books and Grade 4 read 5 1/2×8=44, so the difference is 56−44=12.

y.D: 8 is 8 × 1, the books that one symbol stands for. Grade 5 is one and a half symbols ahead: 56 − 44 = 12 books.

qr.q: Two rectangular pens each use exactly 24 meters of fencing. Pen 1 measures 4 m by 8 m and Pen 2 measures 6 m by 6 m. How much greater is the area of Pen 2?
qr.e: Both perimeters are 24 m, but the areas are 4×8=32 and 6×6=36, so Pen 2 is 36−32=4 square meters larger.

y.A: 0 says the areas are equal. The fencing is — both 24 m — but the areas are 4 × 8 = 32 and 6 × 6 = 36.
y.B: 2 is 4 ÷ 2. The gap between the areas is 36 − 32 = 4.
y.C: 12 is 4 + 8, one long side and one short. The areas are 32 and 36.

qr.q: Bag X holds 4 red and 8 blue marbles. Bag Y holds 3 red and 5 blue marbles. From which bag is drawing a red marble more likely?
c: Bag X, because it has more red marbles
Bag X, because it holds more marbles in all
Bag Y, because 3/8 is greater than 1/3
qr.e: Bag X gives 4/12=1/3 and Bag Y gives 3/8; since 1/3=8/24 and 3/8=9/24, Bag Y is more likely.

qr.q: A rug is 6 feet long and 4 feet wide. A second rug is 3 times as long and half as wide as the first. How does the area of the second rug compare with the area of the first?
qr.e: The first rug covers 6×4=24 sq ft; the second is 18 by 2, or 36 sq ft, and 36÷24=1 1/2. Tripling one side and halving the other multiplies the area by 3×1/2.

qr.q: The mean of five numbers is 14. A sixth number is added, and the mean of all six numbers is 15. What is the sixth number?
qr.e: The five numbers total 5×14=70 and all six total 6×15=90, so the added number is 90−70=20.

qr.q: In a triangle, two of the angles are equal and the third angle is 30° larger than each of them. What is the measure of the largest angle?
qr.e: If each equal angle is x, then x+x+(x+30)=180, so 3x=150 and x=50; the largest angle is 50+30=80°.

y.C: 50 is 80 − 30, the size of each of the two equal angles. The largest angle is 30° bigger than those: 50 + 30 = 80°.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 5?
qr.e: A whole number is divisible by 5 when its last digit is 0 or 5, and 75 ends in 5 while the others end in 2, 8, and 4.

qr.q: A rope is 4 feet long. How many inches long is the rope? (1 foot = 12 inches)
qr.e: Each foot is 12 inches, so 4 feet is 4 × 12 = 48 inches.

y.A: 24 is 12 × 2, two feet of rope. There are four: 4 × 12 = 48.
y.B: 16 is 4 + 12. Each foot holds 12 inches, so the feet multiply: 4 × 12 = 48.
y.C: 44 is 48 − 4, four inches short. Four feet is 4 × 12 = 48.

qr.q: A printer prints 42 pages in 6 minutes at a steady rate. How many pages does it print in 15 minutes?
qr.e: The rate is 42÷6=7 pages per minute, so in 15 minutes it prints 7×15=105 pages.

y.B: 90 is 6 × 15, the two times multiplied. Find the rate first: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 a minute, so 7 × 15 = 105.
y.C: 63 is 105 − 42. The printer does 7 pages a minute, so 15 minutes is 7 × 15 = 105.
y.D: 84 is 42 × 2, which is 12 minutes’ worth. Fifteen minutes is 7 × 15 = 105.

qr.q: The numbers in a pattern are 45, 40, 35, 30, ... . What is the next number in the pattern?
qr.e: Each number is 5 less than the one before it, so the next number is 30 − 5 = 25.

qr.q: A jacket priced at $80 is marked down 25%. At the register, another $5 is taken off. What is the final price?
qr.e: 25% of $80 is $20, so the marked-down price is $60, and $60−$5=$55.

y.D: 60 is 55 + 5, the price after the 25% comes off but before the $5 at the register. That last $5 still has to go: $60 − $5 = $55.

qr.q: A team records its goals each week: Week 1 has 4 goals, Week 2 has 7 goals, Week 3 has 5 goals, and Week 4 has 6 goals. How many goals did the team score in the four weeks altogether?
qr.e: Adding the four weeks gives 4 + 7 + 5 + 6 = 22 goals.

y.A: 23 is 22 + 1, one goal too many. The four weeks are 4 + 7 + 5 + 6 = 22.
y.B: 21 is 22 − 1, one short. Adding the four weeks gives 22.
y.C: 26 is 4 + 22, the first week counted twice. The total is 22.

qr.q: Ten cards numbered 1 through 10 are placed face down and one is drawn at random. What is the probability that the card drawn shows a prime number?
qr.e: The primes from 1 to 10 are 2, 3, 5, and 7 — four of the ten cards — so the probability is 4/10=2/5.

qr.q: Which fraction is between 1/3 and 1/2?
qr.e: In twelfths, 1/3=4/12 and 1/2=6/12, and 5/12 falls between them; 1/4 is smaller and 3/5 and 2/3 are larger than 1/2.

qr.q: Priya has 5/8 of a yard of ribbon but needs 2/3 of a yard. How much more ribbon does she need?
qr.e: Using 24ths, 2/3=16/24 and 5/8=15/24, so she needs 16/24−15/24=1/24 of a yard.

qr.q: A rectangular sheet of paper is 10 cm by 6 cm. A 3 cm by 4 cm rectangle is cut away from one corner. What is the area of the piece that is left?
qr.e: The whole sheet is 10×6=60 square cm and the piece removed is 3×4=12, so 60−12=48 square cm remain.

y.A: 60 is 10 × 6, the area of the whole sheet before the corner was cut away. The piece taken out comes off: 60 − 12 = 48 square cm.

qr.q: Three vertices of a rectangle are (1, 5), (9, 5), and (9, 2). What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex?
qr.e: The fourth vertex shares the x-value 1 with (1, 5) and the y-value 2 with (9, 2), giving (1, 2).

qr.q: A stadium sold 4,180 tickets on Friday, 3,905 on Saturday, and 2,870 on Sunday. Which is the best estimate of the total number of tickets sold?
qr.e: Rounding gives 4,200+3,900+2,900=11,000, and the exact total, 10,955, is much closer to 11,000 than to 10,000.

qr.q: Three pencils and two erasers cost $1.30 in all. One pencil costs $0.30. What does one eraser cost?
qr.e: The pencils cost 3×$0.30=$0.90, leaving $1.30−$0.90=$0.40 for two erasers, so one eraser is $0.20.

y.A: 0.15 is 0.30 ÷ 2, half the price of one pencil. The halving belongs to what is left after the pencils: $1.30 − $0.90 = $0.40, and $0.40 ÷ 2 = $0.20.
y.D: 0.40 is 0.20 × 2, what the two erasers cost together. One eraser is half of that: $0.40 ÷ 2 = $0.20.

qr.q: A student's five test scores have a mean of 82. If the lowest score, 62, is dropped, what is the mean of the four remaining scores?
qr.e: The five scores total 5×82=410; without the 62 the total is 348, and 348÷4=87.

qr.q: In a class, the ratio of students who walk to school to students who ride is 2:5. There are 21 more riders than walkers. How many students are in the class?
qr.e: The difference is 5−2=3 parts, so one part is 21÷3=7 students; the class has 2+5=7 parts, or 7×7=49 students.

qr.q: There are 38 cookies packed into bags of 5. After all the full bags are made, how many cookies are left over?
qr.e: Seven full bags use 7 × 5 = 35 cookies, and 38 − 35 = 3 cookies are left over.

y.C: 2 is 5 − 3, how many more cookies it would take to fill one more bag. The question asks what is left over: seven full bags use 35, and 38 − 35 = 3.

qr.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices, and 3 of the slices are eaten. What fraction of the pizza is left?
qr.e: Three of the 8 slices are gone, so 8 − 3 = 5 slices remain, which is 5/8 of the pizza.

qr.q: Dana has $20 and wants to buy items priced $6.85, $4.20, and $7.95. Which statement is true?
c: She can buy all three and have $1.00 left
She can buy all three with exactly $0 left
She can buy all three and have $2.00 left

qr.q: Which is the best estimate of 4,982 ÷ 51?
qr.e: Rounding gives 5,000÷50=100, and the exact quotient is a little under 98, so 100 is the closest estimate.

qr.q: Four friends have a mean score of 20 in a game. A fifth friend joins with a score of 25. What is the mean score of all five friends?
qr.e: The four friends total 4×20=80, so all five total 105, and 105÷5=21.

qr.q: How many 1-centimeter cubes are needed to fill a box that is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 2 cm tall?
qr.e: Each layer holds 5 × 3 = 15 cubes and the box is 2 layers tall, so 15 × 2 = 30 cubes fill it.

y.A: 60 is 30 × 2, the box counted twice. 5 × 3 × 2 = 30.
y.C: 15 is 5 × 3, one layer. The box is 2 layers tall, so 15 × 2 = 30.
y.D: 10 is 5 × 2, the length and the height. The width is needed too: 5 × 3 × 2 = 30.

qr.q: On a scale drawing, 3 cm represents 12 meters. A hallway is actually 30 meters long. How long is that hallway on the drawing?
qr.e: Since 3 cm stands for 12 m, 1 cm stands for 4 m, so 30 m needs 30÷4=7.5 cm.

y.A: 9 is 3 × 3. One centimetre stands for 4 m, so 30 m needs 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5 cm.
y.B: 10 is 30 ÷ 3, dividing by the centimetres instead of the metres. Each centimetre is 4 m: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5.
y.D: 2.5 is 30 ÷ 12, using the 12 on its own. Three centimetres stand for 12 m, so one stands for 4 m.

qr.q: Car A travels 150 miles on 5 gallons of gas. Car B travels 210 miles on 7 gallons. Which car goes farther on one gallon?
c: Car A, at 35 miles per gallon
Car B, at 30 miles per gallon
Car B, because it traveled more miles
Neither — both travel 30 miles per gallon
qr.e: 150÷5=30 and 210÷7=30, so the two cars have exactly the same rate of 30 miles per gallon.

y.A: Car A, at 35 miles per gallon — 35 is 5 × 7, the two gallon amounts multiplied together. A rate comes from dividing: 150 ÷ 5 = 30, and Car B gives 210 ÷ 7 = 30 as well.
y.B: Car B, at 30 miles per gallon — 30 is 210 ÷ 7, which is right for Car B. Car A works out at the same rate, 150 ÷ 5 = 30, so neither car goes farther.

qr.q: A spinner has 20 equal sections, and each section is either green or white. The probability of landing on green is 2/5. How many of the sections are white?
qr.e: Two fifths of the 20 sections is 8 green sections, so the other 20 − 8 = 12 sections are white.

y.A: 15 is 20 − 5, taking off the 5 from the fraction rather than the green sections. Two fifths of 20 is 8, so white is 12.
y.B: 10 is 20 ÷ 2, half the spinner. Two fifths of 20 is 8 green, leaving 12 white.
y.D: 8 is the green sections. The question asks for the white ones: 20 − 8 = 12.

qr.q: A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The rectangle measures 12 cm by 4 cm. What is the area of the square?
qr.e: The rectangle's perimeter is 2(12+4)=32 cm, so the square has side 32÷4=8 cm and area 8×8=64 square cm.

y.A: 48 is 12 × 4, the rectangle’s area. The question asks for the square’s.
y.B: 32 is the perimeter the two shapes share, not an area. The square’s side is 32 ÷ 4 = 8.
y.D: 16 is 12 + 4. The square’s side is 32 ÷ 4 = 8, so its area is 8 × 8 = 64.

qr.q: The $60 price of a game is raised by 10%, and the new price is later lowered by 10%. What is the final price?
qr.e: The price rises to $66, and 10% of $66 is $6.60, so the final price is $66−$6.60=$59.40 — less than the original because the second 10% is taken from a larger number.

qr.q: Elena spent 2/5 of her money on a book, then spent 1/3 of what was left on a snack. She has $12 left. How much money did she start with?
qr.e: After the book, 3/5 remains; spending 1/3 of that leaves 2/3 × 3/5 = 2/5 of the start, so 2/5 of the money is $12 and the whole is $30.

y.A: 24 is 12 × 2. What she has left is two fifths of the start, so one fifth is 6 and the start was 30.
y.B: 20 is 5 × 4. Twelve dollars is two fifths of the start, so a fifth is 6 and the start was 30.
y.D: 36 is 12 × 3. Two fifths is what is left, so a fifth is 6 and she began with 30.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is the greatest?
qr.e: Written as decimals, 3/5=0.6 and 2/3 is about 0.667, so 0.7 is greater than all the others, including 0.68.

qr.q: In a survey, 35 out of 50 students chose soccer. What percent of the students chose soccer?
qr.e: 35/50 = 70/100, so 70% of the students chose soccer.

y.A: 35 is the number of students who chose soccer, a count out of 50 rather than a percentage. Percent means out of 100: doubling both numbers turns 35 out of 50 into 70 out of 100.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is NOT divisible by 6?
qr.e: A number divisible by 6 must be even and have a digit sum divisible by 3; 358 is even but 3+5+8=16 is not a multiple of 3, while 132, 246, and 414 pass both tests.

qr.q: A list of numbers is 3, 7, 3, 9, and 5. What is the mode of the list?
qr.e: The mode is the value that appears most often, and 3 appears twice while each of the others appears once.

y.A: 9 is the largest number in the list, not the one that turns up most often. The mode counts repeats: 3 appears twice and every other number once.

qr.q: What is the median of 4, 9, 11, 15, 6, and 20?
qr.e: In order the values are 4, 6, 9, 11, 15, 20; with six values the median is the mean of the middle two, (9+11)÷2=10.

y.A: 11 is the fourth value once they are in order. With six values the median sits between the third and fourth, 9 and 11.
y.B: 9 is the third value in order. Six values have no single middle, so take 9 and 11 and halve: 10.
y.D: 13 is 4 + 9, two of the values added. In order they run 4, 6, 9, 11, 15, 20, and the middle two make 10.

qr.q: A number pattern counts by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, ... . What is the 6th number in the pattern?
qr.e: Counting on by 3s gives 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, so the 6th number in the pattern is 18.

y.A: 24 is the 8th number, two steps too far. The 6th is 18.
y.C: 21 is the 7th number, one step too far. The 6th is 18.
y.D: 15 is the 5th number, one step short. The 6th is 18.

qr.q: How many cubes with edges of 2 cm fit exactly inside a box that is 8 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm?
qr.e: Along the edges the cubes fit 4 by 3 by 2, so 4×3×2=24 cubes fill the box.

y.B: 12 is 6 × 2. Count cubes along every edge: 4, 3 and 2, so 4 × 3 × 2 = 24.
y.C: 96 is 24 × 4, four times as many as fit.
y.D: 48 is 8 × 6, two sides in centimetres. The cubes are 2 cm, so the edges hold 4, 3 and 2 of them.

qr.q: Which of these numbers is a factor of 15?
qr.e: 15 = 3 × 5, so 5 divides 15 with nothing left over, while 2, 4, and 6 do not.

qr.q: Two angles are complementary, and one of them is twice as large as the other. What is the measure of the larger angle?
qr.e: Complementary angles total 90°, so x+2x=90 gives x=30° and the larger angle is 2×30=60°.

qr.q: Which is greater, 3 × 3 × 3 or 5 × 5, and by how much?
A jar holds 15 buttons: 6 are blue, 4 are white, and 5 are black. One button is taken out without looking. What is the probability that it is black?
qr.e: There are 15 buttons in all and 5 of them are black, so the probability is 5/15, which is the same as 1/3.

qr.q: Five boxes each hold the same number of books. When 3 more books are added to the collection, there are 43 books in all. How many books are in each box?
qr.e: If each box holds b books, then 5b+3=43, so 5b=40 and b=8.

qr.q: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width. If the perimeter is 48 cm, what is the width?
qr.e: With width w the length is 3w, so the perimeter is 2(3w+w)=8w=48, giving w=6 cm (and length 18 cm).

y.A: 8 is 48 ÷ 6. The perimeter here is eight widths, so the width is 48 ÷ 8 = 6.
y.C: 12 is 6 × 2, two widths. The width itself is 6.
y.D: 18 is 3 × 6, the length, not the width.

qr.q: Notebooks cost $2.95 each. Maya has $20 and no coupon. What is the greatest number of notebooks she can buy?
qr.e: Rounding $2.95 up to $3 gives about 6 notebooks; checking, 6 cost $17.70 and 7 would cost $20.65, which is more than $20.

qr.q: A rectangular pool measures 10 m by 6 m. A walkway 2 m wide is built all the way around it. What is the area of the walkway alone?
qr.e: The pool plus walkway measures 14 m by 10 m, or 140 square meters, and the pool covers 60, so the walkway is 140−60=80 square meters.

y.C: 60 is 10 × 6, the area of the pool itself. The walkway is the ring around it: the pool and walkway together are 14 m by 10 m, so 140 − 60 = 80 square metres.

ma.e: Add by place value to get 4,150.

ma.q: What is 315 ÷ 7?
Of 36 theater seats, two thirds are filled. How many seats are filled?

y.C: 18 is 36 ÷ 2, half the seats rather than two thirds of them. Split the 36 into three first: 36 ÷ 3 = 12, then 12 × 2 = 24.

ma.q: Three quarters of a gallon fills how many one-eighth-gallon jars?
ma.e: 3/4 = 6/8, so there are six eighths.

ma.q: What is 6.4 × 0.5?
ma.e: Multiplying by 0.5 means taking half.

y.A: 12.8 is 6.4 ÷ 0.5, the 6.4 divided by the half rather than multiplied by it. Multiplying by 0.5 takes half, and half of the 6.4 comes to 3.2.

ma.q: An $8.75 fare is reduced by a $3.90 coupon. What is the new fare?
Thirty percent of 90 campers choose chess. How many campers?
What is 40% of 70?

y.B: 30 is 70 − 40, the forty taken off the seventy rather than used as a percentage. Forty per cent means four tenths: 70 ÷ 10 = 7, then 7 × 4 = 28.

ma.q: What is 7 + 3 × 9?
ma.e: Multiply first, then add, to get 34.

ma.q: What is 5/6 - 1/3?
ma.e: 1/3 = 2/6; the difference is 3/6 = 1/2.
Add by place value to get 6,350.

ma.q: What is 750 ÷ 10?
What is 3/8 + 1/4?
ma.e: 1/4 = 2/8, so the sum is 5/8.

ma.q: An 8.75 m ribbon loses 3.9 m of trim. What length remains?
Thirty percent of 90 badges are blue. How many badges?

ma.e: Add by place value to get 7,450.

ma.q: What is 720 ÷ 8?
What is 6 + 4 × 8?
ma.e: Multiply first, then add, to get 38.

ma.q: A 36-card deck has two thirds picture cards. How many picture cards are there?

y.D: 18 is 36 ÷ 2, half the deck rather than two thirds of it. Split the 36 into three first: 36 ÷ 3 = 12, then 12 × 2 = 24.

ma.q: What is 7.2 ÷ 0.6?
ma.e: Multiply both numbers by 10: 72 ÷ 6 = 12.

y.B: 1.2 is 0.6 × 2, the 0.6 doubled rather than divided into the 7.2. Make both numbers ten times bigger first: 72 ÷ 6 = 12.

ma.q: What is 20% of 80?

y.D: 60 is 80 − 20, the twenty taken off the eighty rather than used as a percentage. Twenty per cent means two tenths: 80 ÷ 10 = 8, then 8 × 2 = 16.

ma.q: What is 630 ÷ 6?

ma.e: Add by place value to get 8,990.

ma.q: Three quarters of a yard makes how many one-eighth-yard strips?
ma.e: 3/4 = 6/8, so there are six eighths.

ma.q: A garden is 6 m by 3 m. What fencing length goes around it?
ma.e: Perimeter = 2(6+3) = 18 m.

y.A: 9 is 6 + 3 — one long side and one short one. The fence goes round all four.
y.B: 12 is 6 + 6, the two long sides, with the short ones missing.
y.D: 15 is 6 + 6 + 3 — one short side left out.

ma.q: A triangular flag has base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?

y.B: 60 is 10 × 6, the base times the height — the whole rectangle around the triangle. The triangle fills half of it: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.
y.D: 16 is 10 + 6, the base and the height added rather than multiplied. Multiply them and take half: 10 × 6 = 60, then 60 ÷ 2 = 30.

ma.q: A roof triangle has angles 45° and 60°. What is its third angle?
ma.e: Triangle angles total 180°: the third angle is 75°.

ma.q: A square patio has side length 10 units. What is its area?

y.A: 110 is 100 + 10 — the area with one more side added on the end. The area is just 10 × 10.
y.B: 40 is 10 × 4, the perimeter: the distance all the way round the patio, not the space inside it.
y.C: 20 is 10 × 2, two sides. Area covers the whole patio, so it is 10 × 10.

ma.q: A banner is 10 cm by 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
ma.e: Perimeter = 2(10+3) = 26 cm.

y.A: 13 is 10 + 3, only two of the four sides.
y.B: 30 is 10 × 3, the area. Area is the space inside the banner; perimeter is the distance round its edge.
y.D: 23 is 10 + 10 + 3 — one short side left out.

ma.q: A triangular flag has base 10 cm and height 8 cm. What is its area?

y.A: 80 is 10 × 8, the whole rectangle the triangle sits in. A triangle fills half of it, so halve it: 40.
y.B: 18 is 10 + 8. Area multiplies the base and the height, it never adds them.
y.D: 48 is 40 + 8, the area with the height added on again. Once you have half of 10 × 8 you are done.

ma.q: A sail triangle has angles 65° and 55°. What is its third angle?
ma.e: Triangle angles total 180°: the third angle is 60°.

ma.q: A square mosaic has side length 7 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area = 7² = 49.

y.A: 28 is 7 × 4, the perimeter — the distance round all four sides, not the space inside.
y.C: 14 is 7 × 2, two sides. Area covers the whole square: 7 × 7.
y.D: 56 is 49 + 7, the area with one more side added on. 7 × 7 = 49 is all of it.

ma.q: A pen is 8 cm by 3 cm. What is its perimeter?
ma.e: Perimeter = 2(8+3) = 22 cm.

y.B: 19 is 8 + 8 + 3 — one short side is missing.
y.C: 24 is 8 × 3, the area. That is the ground the pen covers, not the fence around it.
y.D: 11 is 8 + 3, one long side and one short one.

ma.q: A triangular sign has base 10 cm and height 4 cm. What is its area?

y.A: 14 is 10 + 4, the base and the height added rather than multiplied. Multiply them and take half: 10 × 4 = 40, then 40 ÷ 2 = 20.
y.B: 40 is 10 × 4, the base times the height — the whole rectangle around the triangle. The triangle fills half of it: 40 ÷ 2 = 20.

ma.q: A roof triangle has angles 45° and 75°. What is its third angle?
ma.e: Triangle angles total 180°: the third angle is 60°.

ma.q: A square game board has side length 4 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area = 4² = 16.

y.A: 20 is 16 + 4, the area with a side added on the end. The area is just 4 × 4.
y.B: 12 is 16 − 4. Nothing is taken off an area: 4 × 4 = 16.
y.C: 8 is 4 × 2, two sides. A square has four, and its area is 4 × 4.

ma.q: A $100 item is 75% off. What is its sale price?
What is 5.5÷0.1?
ma.e: Dividing by 0.1 makes the number ten times as large: 55.

ma.q: Solve 3x+5=83.
ma.e: Subtract 5, then divide by 3: x=26.

ma.q: Four tenths of 70 teams earn a badge. How many teams earn a badge?
ma.e: Four tenths of 70 is 28.

ma.q: A square stage has side length 9 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area=9²=81.

y.B: 18 is 9 × 2, two sides. Area is 9 × 9.
y.C: 36 is 9 × 4, the perimeter — round the edge, not the space inside.
y.D: 90 is 81 + 9, the area with one more side added on. 9 × 9 = 81 is all of it.

ma.q: What is 160÷2?
ma.e: Half of 160 is 80.

ma.q: What is 25% of 88?
ma.e: One fourth of 88 is 22.

ma.q: What is 7×6?
What is 3/4 of 48?

y.A: 24 is 48 ÷ 2, half of the forty-eight rather than three quarters of it. Quarter it first: 48 ÷ 4 = 12, then 12 × 3 = 36.
y.D: 12 is 48 ÷ 4, one quarter of the forty-eight rather than three quarters of it. Three quarters means three of those quarters: 12 × 3 = 36.

ma.q: What is 5×13?
2.5 feet equals how many inches?
What is 7×8?

y.B: 64 is 8 × 8, eight eights rather than seven. Take one eight away: 64 − 8 = 56.

ma.q: A storage box measures 6×2×2. What is its volume?
A poster is 3 feet long. How many inches is that?
ma.e: 3 × 12 = 36 inches.

y.D: 9 is 3 × 3, the three feet tripled rather than turned into inches. A foot is 12 inches, so 3 × 12 = 36.

ma.q: What is the mean of daily readings 54, 58, and 62?
ma.e: The sum is 174; divide by 3 to get 58.

ma.q: What is the median of 53,56,59,62,66?
ma.e: The ordered middle value is 59.

ma.q: Which value is the mode of 56,59,59,61,64?
ma.e: 59 occurs most often.

ma.q: An aquarium measures 6×3×4. What is its volume?
An 8-foot rope is how many inches long?
ma.e: 8 × 12 = 96 inches.

ma.q: What is the mean of readings 59,63,67?
ma.e: The sum is 189; divide by 3 to get 63.

ma.q: What is the median of 58,61,64,67,71?
ma.e: The ordered middle value is 64.

ma.q: Which value is the mode of 61,64,64,66,69?
ma.e: 64 occurs most often.

ma.q: A bag holds 4 red and 6 blue marbles. What is P(red)?
ma.e: There are 10 marbles and 4 are red: 4/10.

ma.q: A crate measures 7×5×4. What is its volume?

y.D: 16 is 4 × 4, the 4 multiplied by itself rather than by the other two sides. Volume uses all three: 7 × 5 = 35, then 35 × 4 = 140.

ma.q: A block measures 3×2×2. What is its volume?
An 8-foot banner is how many inches long?
ma.e: 8 × 12 = 96 inches.

ma.q: Which value is the mode of 66,69,69,71,74?
ma.e: 69 occurs most often.

ma.q: What is the mean of 67,71,75?
ma.e: The sum is 213; divide by 3 to get 71.

ma.q: What is the median of 66,69,72,75,79?
ma.e: The ordered middle value is 72.

ma.q: A bag holds 3 red and 3 blue marbles. What is P(red)?
ma.e: There are 6 marbles and 3 are red: 3/6.

ma.q: A box measures 4×4×2. What is its volume?
A 7-foot curtain is how many inches long?
ma.e: 7 × 12 = 84 inches.

ma.q: Which value is the mode of 72,75,75,77,80?
ma.e: 75 occurs most often.

ma.q: What is the mean of 73,77,81?
ma.e: The sum is 231; divide by 3 to get 77.

ma.q: What is the median of 72,75,78,81,85?
ma.e: The ordered middle value is 78.

ma.q: A bag holds 5 red and 4 blue marbles. What is P(red)?
ma.e: There are 9 marbles and 5 are red: 5/9.

ma.q: A sheet of paper is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
ma.e: Perimeter is the whole way round: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4 = 26 cm.

y.A: 13 is 9 + 4 — that is only two of the four sides.
y.C: 36 is 9 × 4, which is the area. Area is the space inside the paper; perimeter is the walk around its edge.
y.D: 18 is 9 + 9, the two long sides, with both short ones left out.

ma.q: A rug is 7 feet long and 3 feet wide. A ribbon is sewn all the way around its edge. How long is the ribbon?
ma.e: "All the way around" is the perimeter: 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 feet.

y.A: 10 is 7 + 3 — one long side and one short one. The ribbon goes round all four.
y.B: 14 is 7 + 7, the two long sides only.
y.C: 21 is 7 × 3, the area — how much floor the rug covers, not how far it is round the edge.

ma.q: A square tile has sides of 6 inches. What is its perimeter?
ma.e: Four equal sides: 6 × 4 = 24 inches.

y.B: 12 is two sides. A square has four.
y.C: 18 is three sides — one is still missing.
y.D: 36 is 6 × 6, the area of the tile, not the distance round it.

ma.q: A rectangular garden has an area of 24 square metres. It is 4 metres wide. How long is it?
ma.e: Area = length × width, so length = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 m.

y.A: 5 is one short. Count the fours: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 — that is six of them.
y.B: 12 is half of 24. Halving only gives the answer when the other side is 2.
y.D: 20 is 24 − 4. The two sides were multiplied to make the area, so divide to get one back.

ma.q: A card has an area of 18 square centimetres and is 3 centimetres wide. How tall is it?

y.A: 5 is one short: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 is six threes.
y.B: 9 is half of 18 — right only if the card were 2 cm wide.
y.C: 15 is 18 − 3. Area comes from multiplying, so divide to undo it.

ma.q: A doormat covers 8 square feet. It is 4 feet long. How wide is it?
ma.e: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 feet.

y.A: 1 is one short: 4, then 4 again, makes 8 — two fours fit, not one.
y.C: 4 is 8 − 4. Undo a multiplication by dividing, not subtracting.
y.D: 32 is 8 × 4, which multiplies the area again instead of splitting it.

ma.q: A rectangular photo has a perimeter of 18 inches. It is 6 inches long. How wide is it?
ma.e: Two lengths take 12, leaving 18 − 12 = 6 for the two widths, so each width is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 inches.

y.A: 6 is what is left once both lengths are taken off — but that 6 is TWO widths. Halve it.
y.B: 12 is 18 − 6, which takes off one length when the photo has two.
y.D: 9 is half the perimeter, which is one length plus one width. The 6 still has to come off.

ma.q: A flowerbed is edged with 22 metres of brick. The bed is 7 metres long. How wide is it?
ma.e: Two lengths take 14, leaving 22 − 14 = 8 for the two widths, so each width is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 m.

y.B: 8 is both widths together. One width is half of it.
y.C: 11 is half of 22 — one length plus one width. The 7 still has to come off.
y.D: 15 is 22 − 7, taking off one length when the brick runs along two.

ma.q: If 3x + 7 = 19, what is x?
ma.e: Subtract 7, then divide by 3: x = 4.

y.D: 16 is 19 − 3, the total with the 3 taken off instead of the 7. The 7 comes off first: 19 − 7 = 12, then 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

ma.q: Which bus route number is divisible by both 2 and 3?
ma.e: 24 is even and its digit sum is 6, so it is divisible by 6.

ma.q: A game starts with 8 base points and adds 5 packs of 10 points. What is the total?
ma.e: Multiply first, then add, to get 58.

y.A: 48 is 58 − 10, the total with ten taken off it — one pack of points short. All five packs count: 5 × 10 = 50, then 50 + 8 = 58.
y.C: 63 is 58 + 5, the total with the 5 counted a second time. The 5 is the number of packs, not points of its own: 5 × 10 = 50, then 50 + 8 = 58.

ma.q: Three quarters of a cup makes how many one-eighth-cup samples?
ma.e: 3/4 = 6/8, so there are six eighths.

ma.q: A 6.4-meter ribbon is cut in half. How long is each piece?
ma.e: Cutting in half means multiply by 0.5: 3.2 meters.

y.D: 12.8 is 6.4 × 2, the ribbon doubled rather than halved. Cutting in half means 6.4 ÷ 2 = 3.2 metres for each piece.

ma.q: What is 25% of 64?

y.C: 39 is 64 − 25, the 25 taken away as a plain number rather than used as a per cent. Twenty-five per cent means a quarter: 64 ÷ 4 = 16.

ma.q: A square has side length 5 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area = 5² = 25.

y.B: 20 is 5 × 4, the perimeter — the way round the edge, not the space inside.
y.C: 10 is 5 × 2, two sides. Area is 5 × 5.
y.D: 30 is 25 + 5, the area with a side added on. 5 × 5 = 25 is the answer.

ma.q: What is the volume of a 7 × 5 × 3 rectangular prism?

y.A: 15 is 5 × 3, two of the three sides multiplied — one face of the box, not the space inside it. The 7 still has to come in: 15 × 7 = 105.

ma.q: What is the mean of 84, 88, and 92?
ma.e: The sum is 264; divide by 3 to get 88.

ma.q: If 4x + 6 = 26, what is x?
ma.e: Subtract 6, then divide by 4: x = 5.

y.B: 22 is 26 − 4, the total with the 4 taken off instead of the 6. The 6 comes off first: 26 − 6 = 20, then 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

ma.q: Which locker code has digits that add to 6 and is even?
ma.e: 24 is even and 2+4=6.

ma.q: What is 7 + 6 × 9?
ma.e: Multiply first, then add, to get 61.

y.C: 67 is 61 + 6, the total with the 6 counted a second time. The 6 is only multiplied: 6 × 9 = 54, then 54 + 7 = 61.
y.D: 52 is 61 − 9, the total one nine short. There are six nines to add on: 6 × 9 = 54, then 54 + 7 = 61.

ma.q: If 3x + 9 = 33, what is x?
ma.e: Subtract 9, then divide by 3: x = 8.

y.A: 30 is 33 − 3, the total with the 3 taken off instead of the 9. The 9 comes off first: 33 − 9 = 24, then 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

ma.q: Five sixths of a path is paved, and one third of the whole path is closed. What fraction is paved and open?
What is 2.4 × 0.3?
ma.e: 24 × 3 = 72, then place two decimal digits.

y.B: 8 is 2.4 ÷ 0.3, the two numbers divided rather than multiplied. Multiplying gives 24 × 3 = 72, then two decimal places: 0.72.

ma.q: Forty percent of 70 seedlings sprout. How many seedlings sprout?
A square has side length 8 units. What is its area?
ma.e: Area = 8² = 64.

y.A: 16 is 8 × 2, two sides. Area is 8 × 8.
y.B: 32 is 8 × 4, the perimeter — round the edge, not the space inside.
y.D: 72 is 64 + 8, the area with one more side added on.

ma.q: What is the volume of a 7 × 3 × 4 rectangular prism?
How many inches are in 9 feet?
ma.e: 9 × 12 = 108 inches.

ma.q: What is the mode of 95, 98, 98, 100, 103?
ma.e: 98 occurs most often.

ma.q: A bag has 2 red and 5 blue marbles. What is the probability of red?
ma.e: There are 7 marbles and 2 are red: 2/7.

ma.q: Which number is divisible by 6?
ma.e: 204 is even and its digits sum to 6, so it is divisible by 6.

ma.q: A price is written as 8+5×10. What is its value?
ma.e: Multiply first, then add, to get 58.

y.A: 48 is 58 − 10, the value with ten taken off it — one ten short of the whole. All five tens count: 5 × 10 = 50, then 50 + 8 = 58.
y.C: 63 is 58 + 5, the value with the 5 counted a second time. The 5 only multiplies the 10: 5 × 10 = 50, then 50 + 8 = 58.

ma.q: What is the mean of 99, 103, and 107?
ma.e: The sum is 309; divide by 3 to get 103.

ma.q: Which improper fraction is equal to 3 2/5?
ma.e: A mixed number converts as (3 × 5) + 2 = 17 fifths, so 3 2/5 = 17/5.

ma.q: What is 2/3 + 1/4?
ma.e: Rewrite both with denominator 12: 8/12 + 3/12 = 11/12.

ma.q: What is 7/8 − 2/3?
ma.e: Rewrite with denominator 24: 21/24 − 16/24 = 5/24.

ma.q: What is 3/4 × 2/5?
ma.e: Multiply across: (3 × 2)/(4 × 5) = 6/20, which simplifies to 3/10.

ma.q: What is 5/8 ÷ 1/4?
ma.e: Dividing by 1/4 means multiplying by 4: 5/8 × 4 = 20/8 = 2 1/2.
Change to improper fractions: 5/2 × 8/5 = 40/10 = 4.

ma.q: What is 0.6 × 0.07?
ma.e: 6 × 7 = 42, and the factors have 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places, so the answer is 0.042.

ma.q: What is 4.05 ÷ 0.9?
ma.e: Multiply both numbers by 10: 40.5 ÷ 9 = 4.5. Check: 0.9 × 4.5 = 4.05.

ma.q: What is 7.3 − 2.85?
ma.e: Line up the points and write 7.3 as 7.30: 7.30 − 2.85 = 4.45.

ma.q: Which decimal is equal to 3/8?
Written as a percent, 0.045 is equal to which of the following?
ma.e: Move the decimal point two places right: 0.045 = 4.5%.

ma.q: What is 12.5% of 96?

y.A: 8 is 96 ÷ 12, the 96 split into twelve parts instead. Twelve and a half per cent means an eighth of it: 96 ÷ 8 = 12.

ma.q: A muffin recipe uses 2 3/4 cups of flour for one batch. How many cups of flour are needed for 2 batches?
A pancake recipe calls for 2/3 cup of milk. To make only half of the recipe, how many cups of milk are needed?
ma.e: Half of 2/3 is 1/2 × 2/3 = 2/6, and 2/6 simplifies to 1/3 cup.

ma.q: A pitcher holds 3 1/3 cups of juice. If 5/6 cup is poured out, how many cups of juice remain?
A ribbon 4 1/2 feet long is cut into pieces that are each 3/4 foot long. How many pieces are there?
Apples cost $1.35 per pound. What is the cost of 2.4 pounds of apples?
Ben buys 3 notebooks that cost $2.45 each and pays with a $10 bill. How much change should he receive?

y.D: 7.35 is 3 × 2.45, what the three notebooks cost, not the change. The change is what is left of the $10: 10 − 7.35 = 2.65.

ma.q: A coat is on sale for 30% off its regular price. Rosa pays the sale price of $42. What was the regular price of the coat?
ma.e: The sale price is 100% − 30% = 70% of the regular price, so 10% of the regular price is $42 ÷ 7 = $6, and the whole price is 10 × $6 = $60.

y.D: 72 is 42 + 30, the sale price with the 30 added on as dollars rather than counted as a per cent. Taking 30 per cent off leaves seven tenths of the price, so 42 ÷ 7 = 6 and 6 × 10 = 60.

ma.q: A store raises the price of a $28 board game by 25%. What is the new price?

y.B: 53 is 28 + 25, the 25 added on as dollars rather than counted as a per cent. A quarter of the 28 goes on top: 28 ÷ 4 = 7, then 28 + 7 = 35.

ma.q: A choir has 40 members, and 15 of them play an instrument. What percent of the choir members play an instrument?
A bicycle is marked down from $200 to $150. What is the percent decrease in the price?
ma.e: The drop is $50, and 50/200 = 1/4, so the price decreased by 25%.

y.C: 50 is 200 − 150, the dollars the price fell by, not the per cent it fell by. The drop is measured against the starting price: 50 ÷ 200 gives a quarter, or 25 per cent.

ma.q: Which of these values is the greatest?
ma.e: Written as decimals, 3/5 = 0.6, 5/8 = 0.625 and 58% = 0.58, and 0.625 is more than 0.61, so 5/8 is the greatest value.

ma.q: A tank holds 12.5 liters of water. If 3/5 of the water is used, how many liters remain?
ma.e: The part left is 2/5 of 12.5, and 12.5 ÷ 5 = 2.5, so 2 × 2.5 = 5 liters.

y.A: 6.25 is 12.5 ÷ 2, half of the tank. Two fifths of it is what remains: 12.5 ÷ 5 = 2.5, then 2 × 2.5 = 5.
y.B: 7.5 is 12.5 − 5, the water that was used. The question asks for what is left in the tank: 12.5 − 7.5 = 5 litres.

ma.q: In triangle ABC, angle A measures 34° and angle B is twice as large as angle A. What is the measure of angle C?

y.B: 68 is 34 × 2, the size of angle B, not angle C. All three angles make 180°: 180 − 34 − 68 = 78.

ma.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral measure 100°, 85°, and 65°. What is the measure of the fourth angle?
One acute angle of a right triangle measures 27°. What is the measure of the other acute angle?
ma.e: The two acute angles of a right triangle add to 90°, and 90° − 27° = 63°.

ma.q: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40°, and its two base angles are equal. What is the measure of each base angle?
ma.e: The two base angles share 180° − 40° = 140°, so each one is 140° ÷ 2 = 70°.

y.A: 140 is 70 × 2, the two base angles added together rather than one of them on its own. They share 180 − 40 = 140, so each base angle comes to 140 ÷ 2 = 70.

ma.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 34 cm and a width of 6 cm. What is its length?
ma.e: One length plus one width is 34 ÷ 2 = 17 cm, so the length is 17 − 6 = 11 cm.

y.A: 17 is 34 ÷ 2, one length and one width together. Take the width off it: 17 − 6 = 11.
y.B: 28 is 34 − 6, the whole way round minus one width. Halve the perimeter first, then subtract.
y.C: 22 is 11 × 2, two lengths. The question asks for one.

ma.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 square inches and a length of 9 inches. What is its perimeter?
ma.e: The width is 72 ÷ 9 = 8 in, so the perimeter is 2 × (9 + 8) = 34 in.

y.B: 36 is 9 × 4, as if all four sides were 9. The width is 72 ÷ 9 = 8, not 9.
y.C: 81 is 9 × 9, as if it were a square. The width is 72 ÷ 9 = 8.
y.D: 17 is 34 ÷ 2, one length and one width. The perimeter is both pairs: 2 × 17 = 34.

ma.q: A large rectangle measures 8 cm along the bottom and 5 cm along each side. A small rectangle 3 cm by 2 cm is cut away from one corner of it, leaving an L-shaped tile. What is the area of the L-shaped tile?
ma.e: The whole rectangle covers 8 × 5 = 40 sq cm and the corner piece cut away covers 3 × 2 = 6 sq cm, so the L-shaped tile left over covers 40 − 6 = 34 sq cm.

y.D: 40 is 8 × 5, the whole rectangle before the corner was cut away. The piece cut out still comes off: 40 − 6 = 34 sq cm.

ma.q: Two rectangles each have an area of 36 square units. One measures 6 by 6 and the other measures 12 by 3. How much greater is the perimeter of the 12-by-3 rectangle than the perimeter of the 6-by-6 rectangle?
ma.e: The perimeters are 2 × (12 + 3) = 30 and 2 × (6 + 6) = 24, and 30 − 24 = 6 units.

y.A: 0 says the two perimeters are the same. The areas are — both 36 — but the perimeters are 30 and 24.
y.B: 3 is 6 − 3, one side from each rectangle. The question compares the whole way round both.
y.D: 9 is 6 + 3, one side of each. Going all the way round gives 30 and 24, a gap of 6.

ma.q: A circular tabletop has a radius of 13 inches. What is its diameter?
ma.e: A diameter is twice the radius, so 2 × 13 = 26 in.

y.B: 13 is the radius you started with — the centre to the edge, half the way across.
y.C: 6.5 is 13 ÷ 2. That halves the radius; a diameter doubles it.
y.D: 52 is 26 × 2, the diameter doubled again. One doubling is enough.

ma.q: Point P is located at (7, 5) on a coordinate grid. The point is moved 4 units left and 2 units down. What are the coordinates of its new position?
ma.e: Moving left subtracts from x and moving down subtracts from y: (7 − 4, 5 − 2) = (3, 3).

ma.q: A rectangle on a coordinate grid has vertices at (2, 1), (8, 1), (8, 5), and (2, 5). What is the area of the rectangle, in square units?
ma.e: The rectangle is 8 − 2 = 6 units wide and 5 − 1 = 4 units tall, so the area is 6 × 4 = 24 square units.

y.A: 10 is 2 + 8, two of the across numbers added. The rectangle is 8 − 2 = 6 wide and 5 − 1 = 4 tall, so 6 × 4 = 24.
y.C: 20 is 5 × 4, using a corner number instead of a side. The sides are 6 and 4: 6 × 4 = 24.
y.D: 48 is 24 × 2, the rectangle counted twice. 6 × 4 = 24.

ma.q: The point (2, 5) is reflected across the vertical line x = 6. What are the coordinates of its image?
ma.e: The point is 4 units left of x = 6, so its image is 4 units right of it, at (6 + 4, 5) = (10, 5).

ma.q: A rectangular room measures 12 feet by 9 feet. Carpet costs $3 for each square foot. What is the total cost to carpet the room?
ma.e: The floor area is 12 × 9 = 108 square feet, and 108 × $3 = $324.

y.A: 108 is 12 × 9, the floor area in square feet, not the cost of covering it. Each square foot costs $3: 108 × 3 = 324.

ma.q: A figure is made of a rectangle with a triangle sitting on top of it. The rectangle is 10 cm wide and 6 cm tall. The bottom edge of the triangle is the whole top edge of the rectangle, so the triangle's base is 10 cm, and the triangle is 4 cm tall. What is the total area of the figure?
ma.e: The rectangle covers 10 × 6 = 60 sq cm and the triangle covers 1/2 × 10 × 4 = 20 sq cm, so the whole figure covers 60 + 20 = 80 sq cm.

ma.q: A square and a rectangle each have a perimeter of 40 cm. The rectangle is 14 cm long. How much greater is the area of the square than the area of the rectangle?
ma.e: The square has side 10 cm and area 100 sq cm; the rectangle is 14 cm by 6 cm with area 84 sq cm, and 100 − 84 = 16 sq cm.

y.A: 26 is 40 − 14, what is left of the perimeter after one 14-cm side — a length, not an area. The square's side is 40 ÷ 4 = 10, so it covers 100 sq cm, and the 14-by-6 rectangle covers 84: 100 − 84 = 16 sq cm.

ma.q: A rectangular sandbox measures 7 feet by 5 feet. Edging costs $4 for each foot. How much will it cost to put edging all the way around the sandbox?
ma.e: The distance around is 2 × (7 + 5) = 24 feet, and 24 × $4 = $96.

y.B: 24 is 96 ÷ 4, the distance all the way round in feet, not the cost of edging it. Each foot costs $4: 24 × 4 = $96.
y.D: $48 is 96 ÷ 2, half of the full cost — edging for one long side and one short side, not all four. The whole way round is 24 feet, and 24 × $4 = $96.

ma.q: In a triangle, the second angle measures 20° more than the first angle, and the third angle measures 40°. What is the measure of the largest angle?
ma.e: The first two angles share 180° − 40° = 140°, so the first is (140 − 20) ÷ 2 = 60° and the second is 80°, the largest.

y.A: 60° is 80 − 20, the first angle — the smaller of the pair, not the largest one. The second angle is 20° bigger: 60 + 20 = 80°.
y.B: 100° is 20 + 80, the 20° difference added on to the largest angle instead of to the first one. Adding the 20° to the first angle is what gives the largest: 60 + 20 = 80°.

ma.q: Two angles together form a straight line. One of the angles is 3 times as large as the other. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
ma.e: The two angles total 180°, which is 4 equal parts here, so the smaller angle is 180° ÷ 4 = 45°.

y.D: 135° is 3 × 45, the larger of the two angles — three times the smaller one. The question asks for the smaller: 180 ÷ 4 = 45°.

ma.q: A circular garden has a radius of 11 feet. A straight path runs across the garden through its center, from one edge to the other. How long is the path?
ma.e: A path through the center is a diameter, which is 2 × 11 = 22 ft.

y.A: 44 is 22 × 2, the path doubled again. Across the middle is 2 × 11 = 22.
y.C: 11 is the radius — the centre to the edge, which is half the path.
y.D: 5.5 is 11 ÷ 2. A path across the middle doubles the radius, it does not halve it.

ma.q: The diameter of a large circle is 24 cm. A small circle has a radius that is one third as long as the radius of the large circle. What is the diameter of the small circle?
ma.e: The large radius is 12 cm, so the small radius is 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cm and its diameter is 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

y.A: 12 cm is 24 ÷ 2, the radius of the large circle — the first step, not the answer. A third of it gives the small radius, 4 cm, and doubling that gives the diameter: 2 × 4 = 8 cm.
y.B: 4 cm is 8 ÷ 2, the radius of the small circle — right, but the question asks for its diameter. Double it: 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

ma.q: On a city map, the library is at point (2, 3) and the school is at point (2, 11). Each unit on the map is one block. How many blocks apart are the library and the school?
ma.e: Both points have x = 2, so count along the vertical line: 11 − 3 = 8 blocks.

y.B: 6 is 2 × 3, the library’s two numbers multiplied. Count along the line instead: 11 − 3 = 8.
y.C: 14 is 3 + 11, the two up-numbers added. Distance subtracts them: 11 − 3 = 8.
y.D: 11 is the school’s up-number on its own. The distance between them is 11 − 3 = 8.

ma.q: A playground is drawn on a grid with corners at (1, 2), (9, 2), (9, 7), and (1, 7). A fence is built all the way around it. Each grid unit represents 10 meters. How many meters of fence are needed?
ma.e: The playground is 8 units by 5 units, so the distance around is 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 units, and 26 × 10 = 260 m.

y.C: 130 m is 260 ÷ 2, half of the way round — one long side and one short side, not all four. All the way round is 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 units, and 26 × 10 = 260 m.
y.D: 26 m is 260 ÷ 10, the way round counted in grid squares rather than in metres. Each square stands for 10 metres: 26 × 10 = 260 m.

ma.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(2, 1), B(6, 1), and C(2, 4). The whole triangle slides 5 units right and 3 units up. What are the coordinates of point C after the slide?
ma.e: A slide adds to both coordinates: (2 + 5, 4 + 3) = (7, 7).

ma.q: Mr. Diaz has 24 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular pen. Both side lengths must be whole numbers of meters. What is the greatest area he can enclose?
ma.e: The length and width must add to 12, and 6 × 6 = 36 sq m beats every other pair, such as 5 × 7 = 35 sq m.

y.D: 48 sq m is 24 × 2, the fencing doubled — but fencing measures the way round the pen, not the space inside it. The two side lengths add to 12, and the biggest area they make is 6 × 6 = 36 sq m.

ma.q: Kira's four quiz scores are 78, 85, 91, and 86. What is her mean score?

y.B: 340 is 85 × 4, the four scores added together — the total, not the mean. Share it between the four quizzes: 340 ÷ 4 = 85.

ma.q: A bar graph of raffle tickets sold shows Ana 25, Ben 40, Cara 35, and Dan 20. How many tickets did the four students sell in all?
ma.e: 25 + 40 + 35 + 20 = 120 tickets in all.

y.D: 100 is 120 − 20, the tickets with Dan's 20 left out. All four students count: 25 + 40 + 35 + 20 = 120.

ma.q: What is the median of 26, 15, 31, 19, 12, and 22?
ma.e: In order the values are 12, 15, 19, 22, 26, 31, so the median is the mean of the two middle values: (19 + 22) ÷ 2 = 20.5.

y.D: 19 is 31 − 12, the largest value take away the smallest — the spread of the numbers, not the middle of them. In order they run 12, 15, 19, 22, 26, 31, and with six values the median sits between the middle two: (19 + 22) ÷ 2 = 20.5.

ma.q: A puppy weighs 3 pounds 5 ounces. How many ounces does the puppy weigh? (1 pound = 16 ounces)
ma.e: 3 pounds is 3 × 16 = 48 ounces, and 48 + 5 = 53 ounces.

y.A: 56 is 3 + 53, the weight in ounces with the 3 pounds counted a second time. Those 3 pounds are already in there as 48 ounces: 48 + 5 = 53.
y.D: 48 is 3 × 16, the 3 pounds turned into ounces, without the 5 ounces that come with them. Add them on: 48 + 5 = 53.

ma.q: A spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 through 8. What is the probability that one spin lands on a number greater than 5?
ma.e: Three of the eight sections (6, 7, and 8) are greater than 5, so the probability is 3/8.

ma.q: A table shows books read: Monday 4, Tuesday 7, Wednesday 3, Thursday 8, Friday 6. How many more books were read on Tuesday and Thursday together than on Monday and Wednesday together?
ma.e: Tuesday and Thursday give 7 + 8 = 15 books, Monday and Wednesday give 4 + 3 = 7 books, and 15 − 7 = 8.

y.A: 5 is 8 − 3, Thursday take away Wednesday. Add each pair first: 7 + 8 = 15 and 4 + 3 = 7.
y.B: 7 is 4 + 3, Monday and Wednesday together. That is one pair; the other is 15, so the gap is 8.
y.D: 15 is 7 + 8, Tuesday and Thursday together. The question asks how many more, so take the other pair off: 15 − 7 = 8.

ma.q: The mean of five numbers is 26. Four of the numbers are 18, 22, 29, and 34. What is the fifth number?
ma.e: The five numbers must total 5 × 26 = 130, and 18 + 22 + 29 + 34 = 103, so the fifth number is 130 − 103 = 27.

ma.q: A soup recipe calls for 2 quarts of broth. How many cups of broth is that? (1 quart = 4 cups)
ma.e: Each quart is 4 cups, so 2 quarts is 2 × 4 = 8 cups.

y.A: 6 is 2 + 4. Each quart is 4 cups, so the quarts multiply: 2 × 4 = 8.
y.C: 16 is 4 × 4, four quarts’ worth. There are two: 2 × 4 = 8.
y.D: 4 is the cups in one quart. The recipe asks for two: 2 × 4 = 8.

ma.q: A lunch special comes with one of 3 sandwiches, one of 4 sides, and one of 2 drinks. How many different lunch specials are possible?
ma.e: Each of the 3 sandwiches can go with any of the 4 sides and any of the 2 drinks, so there are 3 × 4 × 2 = 24 different lunch specials.

y.D: 12 is 3 × 4, the sandwiches paired with the sides — right, but the drinks are not in it yet. Each of those 12 can go with either drink: 12 × 2 = 24.

ma.q: A line plot shows the number of pets owned by nine students: 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 5. How many students own more pets than the mode?
ma.e: The mode is 1 because it appears three times, and the students with 2, 2, 3, and 5 pets — 4 students in all — own more than 1.

y.A: 3 is a number of pets in the list, not a number of students. The mode is 1, and four students own more than one.
y.C: 6 is 2 × 3. Count the students above the mode instead: the two with 2, the one with 3 and the one with 5.
y.D: 5 is the largest number of pets anyone owns, not how many students. Four own more than the mode.

ma.q: A movie starts at 1:45 p.m. and lasts 2 hours 40 minutes. At what time does the movie end?
ma.e: 1:45 plus 2 hours is 3:45, and 3:45 plus 40 more minutes is 4:25 p.m.

ma.q: A bag holds 5 green counters, 3 yellow counters, and 4 purple counters. What is the probability of drawing a counter that is NOT yellow?
ma.e: There are 5 + 3 + 4 = 12 counters and 9 of them are not yellow, and 9/12 simplifies to 3/4.

ma.q: Jamal's first three test scores are 82, 91, and 87. What score does he need on his fourth test so that his mean for the four tests is exactly 88?
ma.e: Four tests averaging 88 must total 4 × 88 = 352, and 82 + 91 + 87 = 260, so he needs 352 − 260 = 92.

ma.q: A table shows tickets sold over three weeks. Ana sold 12, then 18, then 14. Ben sold 15, then 9, then 22. Who sold more tickets in all, and by how many?
ma.e: Ana sold 12 + 18 + 14 = 44 and Ben sold 15 + 9 + 22 = 46, so Ben sold 46 − 44 = 2 more.

y.A: 6 is 15 − 9, two of Ben’s weeks. Add all three for each: Ana 44 and Ben 46.
y.B: 4 is 18 − 14, two of Ana’s weeks. The totals are Ana 44 and Ben 46, so Ben is ahead.
y.C: 2 is the right gap with the wrong name on it: Ana sold 44 and Ben sold 46.

ma.q: A soccer practice lasts 1 hour 50 minutes and ends at 6:05 p.m. At what time does the practice start?
ma.e: Going back 1 hour from 6:05 gives 5:05, and going back 50 more minutes gives 4:15 p.m.

ma.q: A jar holds 8 red marbles, 4 blue marbles, and 3 green marbles. One red marble is taken out and not put back. What is the probability that the next marble drawn is red?
ma.e: After one red is removed, 7 of the 14 marbles left are red, and 7/14 = 1/2.

ma.q: In a class of 20 students, the mean number of books read over the summer was 7. How many books did the class read in all?
ma.e: The total equals the mean times the number of students: 7 × 20 = 140 books.

y.A: 27 is 20 + 7, the class and the mean added. A mean is shared out, so it multiplies back: 7 × 20 = 140.
y.B: 70 is 140 ÷ 2, half the books. Every one of the 20 read 7 on average: 7 × 20 = 140.
y.C: 280 is 140 × 2, the total counted twice. 7 × 20 = 140.

ma.q: A cooler holds 3 gallons of lemonade. If 1 gallon = 4 quarts and 1 quart = 4 cups, how many cups of lemonade does the cooler hold?
ma.e: 3 gallons is 3 × 4 = 12 quarts, and 12 quarts is 12 × 4 = 48 cups.

y.B: 24 is 48 ÷ 2, half of the cups the cooler holds. There are two steps, both of them × 4: 3 × 4 = 12 quarts, then 12 × 4 = 48 cups.
y.C: 12 is 3 × 4, the cooler measured in quarts — right, but the question asks for cups. Each quart holds 4 cups: 12 × 4 = 48.

ma.q: In a pictograph, each car symbol stands for 6 cars washed. The Saturday row shows 4 and a half symbols. How many cars were washed on Saturday?
ma.e: Four full symbols stand for 4 × 6 = 24 cars and the half symbol stands for 3 more, so 24 + 3 = 27 cars.

y.C: 24 is 6 × 4, the four full symbols — right, but the half symbol is still to come. It stands for 3 more cars: 24 + 3 = 27.
y.D: 21 is 27 − 6, one whole symbol short — three full symbols and the half, rather than four and the half. The four full symbols come to 24, and the half adds 3: 24 + 3 = 27.

ma.q: A box holds only blue pens and black pens. The probability of picking a blue pen at random is 1/4, and there are 5 blue pens in the box. How many pens are in the box in all?
ma.e: The blue pens are 1/4 of all the pens, so the 5 blue pens are one of four equal groups, giving 4 × 5 = 20 pens in all.

y.B: 15 is 20 − 5, the black pens. The question asks how many pens there are altogether: 4 × 5 = 20.
y.C: 9 is 4 + 5. The 5 blue pens are one of four equal parts, so the parts multiply: 4 × 5 = 20.
y.D: 25 is 5 × 5, five parts of five. A quarter means four parts: 4 × 5 = 20.

ma.q: A rectangular photo frame measures 30 centimeters on one side and 0.5 meter on the other. What is the distance all the way around the frame, in centimeters?
ma.e: 0.5 meter is 50 centimeters, so the distance around is 30 + 50 + 30 + 50 = 160 centimeters.

y.B: 80 is 160 ÷ 2, half of the way round — one short side and one long side, 30 and 50. All four sides count: 30 + 50 + 30 + 50 = 160.
y.C: 130 is 160 − 30, the way round with one of the 30-centimetre sides missed out — three sides instead of four. A rectangle has two of each: 30 + 50 + 30 + 50 = 160.

ma.q: A bar graph shows the minutes Ella practiced piano: Monday 30, Tuesday 45, Wednesday 0, Thursday 60, and Friday 45. What was her mean practice time per day for those five days?
ma.e: The total is 30 + 45 + 0 + 60 + 45 = 180 minutes, and 180 ÷ 5 = 36 minutes per day.

y.C: 45 is the practice on Tuesday, and on Friday too — one day's minutes rather than the average of the five. The five days come to 180 minutes, and 180 ÷ 5 = 36.
y.D: 30 is Monday's practice on its own, one day out of the five rather than the average. The five days come to 180 minutes altogether, and 180 ÷ 5 = 36.

ma.q: Of the 60 students in a survey, 1/4 chose soccer and 1/3 chose basketball. The rest chose swimming. How many students chose swimming?
ma.e: 1/4 of 60 is 15 and 1/3 of 60 is 20, so 60 − 15 − 20 = 25 students chose swimming.

y.B: 20 is the basketball group, a third of the sixty. Swimming is what is left over: 60 − 15 − 20 = 25.
y.C: 30 is 60 ÷ 2, half the students. The two named sports take 15 and 20, leaving 25.
y.D: 35 is 15 + 20, the two named groups together. The rest is the answer: 60 − 35 = 25.
